subject.title: Surface internal system messages in a distinct UI block instead of normal chat bubbles

question: Which runtime-originated messages should be hidden as agent-only input, and which should remain visible through a dedicated system/runtime diagnostic presentation across Control UI/WebChat and TUI?
rationale: Current code has partial hiding and role preservation, but the remaining work decides the product boundary between user chat, assistant chat, agent-only runtime input, and intentionally visible diagnostics.

options.title: Audience metadata plus diagnostic lane
options.body: Adopt a shared audience/provenance contract, hide agent-only internals, and add a dedicated diagnostic presentation for intentionally visible system/runtime notices.

options.title: Presentation-only system styling
options.body: Keep current visibility rules and add distinct Control UI/TUI styling for system-role rows, which is smaller but may preserve the wrong audience boundary.

options.title: Hide internal/system rows
options.body: Route all internal/system rows away from visible chat, reducing confusion but also removing transparency for intentional runtime notices.

recommendation.title: Audience metadata plus diagnostic lane
recommendation.body: Adopt a shared audience/provenance contract, hide agent-only internals, and add a dedicated diagnostic presentation for intentionally visible system/runtime notices.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest current-main routing candidate for the UI/projection paths and the narrow memory-flush fix related to the original example.
